title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is studying sections of the arithmetic fundamental group of M_{0,3} (the 'équation des lacets' / Galois action on pi_1 of P^1-{0,1,inf}). On the previous page a partial section had led him to ask, in a moment of confusion, whether an elliptic curve over Q with j=0 can exist. He knew this must be absurd. This page sets up a precise stack-theoretic dictionary to settle the question.

(27) Let U_{0,3} = P^1 - {0,1,inf} be the Legendre lambda-line and S_3 = SL(2,Z/2) (written as a Gothic S_3 in the manuscript) act on it by the anharmonic group.
- M'_{1,1}, the moduli of elliptic curves modulo the symmetry -1 (the rigidification of M_{1,1} by its generic mu_2), is identified with the quotient stack [U_{0,3}/S_3].
- M_{1,1} is identified with [U_{0,3}/S~_3], where S~_3 is a central extension of S_3 by mu_2 acting on U_{0,3} through S_3. The mu_2 is the generic automorphism -1, so M_{1,1} -> M'_{1,1} is a mu_2-gerbe.
- Both stacks have the same coarse space U_{0,3}/S_3 = E^1, the j-line.
- The phrase 'rel. à Q' signals that over Q the group must be understood relative to the base, i.e. possibly as a twisted finite etale Q-group.

(28) S~_3 = (pi_1 of M_{1,1}) / (pi_1 of U_{0,3}).
- Geometrically this is SL(2,Z) / <<-l_0>>, where l_0 = [[1,2],[0,1]] is the loop around 0.
- Equivalently it is SL(2,Z/4) / K, with K the normal subgroup of order 4 generated by -l_0; the corresponding subgroup of SL(2,Z) is generated by -l_0 and -l_1.
- Verification. Gamma(2)/Gamma(4) is the space of trace-zero 2x2 matrices X mod 2, of order 8, containing -1 = I+2I. The S_3-invariant functional f(X) = a+b+c (for X = [[a,b],[c,a]]) satisfies f(I) = 1, so its kernel K is a normal complement to {+-1}. The image of -l_0 = I+2[[1,1],[0,1]] has f = 0, hence lies in K.
- In SL(2,Z), the preimage of K is the kernel of a character chi of Gamma(2) with chi(-1) = -1 and chi invariant under SL(2,Z). It is torsion-free, maps isomorphically onto Gamma(2)/{+-1} (free of rank 2, i.e. pi_1(U_{0,3})), and equals <-l_0, -l_1>, the normal closure of -l_0.
- So S~_3 has order 12, is a non-split central extension of S_3 by mu_2, and is the binary dihedral (dicyclic) group Dic_3.

(29)-(30) Points over Q in this dictionary:
- A point of M'_{1,1} is an S_3-torsor T over Q together with an S_3-equivariant map T -> U_{0,3}. T is the torsor of frames of 2-division points.
- A point of M_{1,1} is an S~_3-torsor T~ with an equivariant map T~ -> U_{0,3}. T~ is the torsor of Jacobi 'fourth roots', a structure intermediate between level 2 and level 4.
- Since T = T~/mu, giving (30) is equivalent to giving (29) plus a lift of T to T~.

Next page: lifting a homomorphism Pi_Q -> S_3 to Pi_Q -> S~_3 has obstruction in H^2(Q, mu_2) = Br(Q)[2]. He then analyses the j=0 point, whose image {-j, -jbar} is connected over Q, so that Pi_Q -> S_3 has image of order 2.

Purpose: translate 'sections of pi_1(M_{0,3}) over Gal(Qbar/Q)' into concrete elliptic curves, and locate exactly where the gerbe M_{1,1} -> M'_{1,1} can obstruct.
errors: The doubt carried over from the previous page (that no elliptic curve over Q with j=0 might exist) is unfounded. The gerbe M_{1,1} -> M'_{1,1} is neutral on every field point. A field point of M'_{1,1} is a P^1 with a rational point and a branch divisor, and a double cover y^2 = f(x) always exists. For example y^2 = x^3+1 has j=0 over Q. So the Br(Q)[2] obstruction set up on the next page must vanish; the earlier puzzle comes from an incorrectly chosen section or lift, not from arithmetic.

Over Q, S~_3 cannot in general be taken as a constant group acting on U_{0,3} compatibly with the Q-structure. For instance, the plain Legendre family is not S_3-equivariant over Q: lambda -> 1-lambda requires a twist by -1, and lambda -> 1/lambda a twist by lambda. Grothendieck's 'rel. à Q' indicates awareness of this, but the identification (27) over Q needs a suitably twisted family or a twisted form of S~_3. This is left implicit.

Minor wording: 'sous-groupe invariant engendré par -l_0' and 'groupe engendré par -l_0, -l_1' describe the same free subgroup only after one checks that the normal closure of -l_0 equals <-l_0, -l_1>. This is true, since the S-conjugate of -l_0 is -l_1^{-1}, but it is unstated.

ideas.what: Presentation of M_{1,1} as the quotient stack of the Legendre lambda-line U_{0,3} by a group of order 12 (a central extension of S_3 by mu_2, acting through S_3), and of M'_{1,1} (rigidified) as [U_{0,3}/S_3], with common coarse space the j-line
ideas.modern_name: Legendre presentation of M_{1,1}[1/2]; rigidification M_{1,1} -> M_{1,1} rigidified by mu_2 as a mu_2-gerbe
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (Deligne-Rapoport-era level structures; stack rigidification formalised by Abramovich-Corti-Vistoli 2003)
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche and the Esquisse discuss M_{1,1} and its relation to M_{0,4}; not this explicit presentation as far as known

ideas.what: Identification of the quotient group as SL(2,Z)/<<-l_0>>, isomorphic to SL(2,Z/4)/(order 4 normal subgroup), i.e. a torsion-free normal free subgroup <-l_0,-l_1> of SL(2,Z) of index 12 mapping isomorphically onto Gamma(2)/{+-1}; quotient is the dicyclic group of order 12
ideas.modern_name: a normal, torsion-free, level-4 congruence complement of {+-1} in Gamma(2); binary dihedral group Dic_3
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical / folklore (congruence subgroups of level 4, Klein-Fricke)

ideas.what: Points of M_{1,1} and M'_{1,1} over Q as torsors (S_3-torsor of 2-division frames; its mu_2-lift to the torsor of Jacobi 'fourth roots') with equivariant maps to U_{0,3}; lifting obstruction in H^2(Q,mu_2) = Br(Q)[2]
ideas.modern_name: torsor description of points of quotient stacks; gerbe lifting obstruction / Brauer class of a mu_2-gerbe

missed.claim: Explicit identification of the intermediate level-4 structure giving a degree-12 Galois etale cover U_{0,3} -> M_{1,1} with group SL(2,Z)/<<-l_0>> (Dic_3), interpreted as Jacobi 'fourth roots', used to make the section conjecture for M_{0,3} versus M_{1,1} concrete. This is folklore-level and mildly nice, but not new mathematics.
missed.quote: S~_3 = S^+/pi_0 ≃ SL(2,Z)/sous-groupe invariant engendré par -l_0 ≃ SL(2,Z/4Z)/sous-groupe (d'ordre 4) engendré par -l_0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical detail on how Grothendieck tested anabelian/section ideas on M_{1,1} via M_{0,3}, i.e. comparing sections of pi_1 of the stack with sections of pi_1 of its rigidification.

deep.surprise_reason: The computations are correct and rather elegant: a normal free index-12 subgroup of SL(2,Z), and M_{1,1} as the Legendre line mod Dic_3. However, this is standard level-structure and gerbe material known to specialists. The page mainly clears up his own momentary confusion about j=0 curves over Q.
transcription_corrections: The group symbol written 'Γ_3' / 'G_3' is a Gothic S: 𝔖_3 (the symmetric group), identified with SL(2,Z/2Z); its extension is 𝔖~_3.
'l'extension de Γ_3 par γ' should read 'par μ' (i.e. μ_2), consistent with T = T~/μ later on the page.
'Γ^+_·/π_0' is probably the arithmetic/geometric pi_1 of M_{1,1} modulo pi_1 of U_{0,3}; the exact decoration is unclear.

Marginal note is roughly: 'T est le torseur SL(2,Z/2) des repères de points de 2-division, T~ celui des "racines quatrièmes" de Jacobi ... (le premier est attaché à ..., le second à une courbe elliptique)'.
'U_{0,3}/Γ_3 ≃ U_{0,3}/Γ~_3' is correct as written (same coarse quotient), with 𝔖 in place of Γ.
